source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Built a text-only Digit Matrices task with the same rule structure as Raven SPM (constant, distribution-of-3, progression; AND/OR/XOR logic). GPT-3 zero-shot, no examples, beat the human mean.
numbers: Humans N=40 UCLA undergrads. Generative answers: GPT-3 vs human odds ratio 1.88, p=0.005, CI [1.21,2.91]. Multiple choice: OR 6.27, p=2.3e-8. Best human got every item right.
limits: Text digits remove visual perception; the novelty claim was later challenged (see counterfactual study). Older GPT-3 only.
agent_relevance: S0 gate: a model can induce the rule type from a text matrix zero-shot, so the hard part is perception and robustness, not rule induction in the clean case.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: GPT-3 showed human-like difficulty signatures on Digit Matrices: progression harder than constant/distribute; more unique rules harder; permuted logic items harder than aligned.
numbers: Progression vs none: human OR 0.41 (p=0.0001), GPT-3 OR 0.07 (p=1.9e-5). Unique rules: human OR 0.61, GPT-3 OR 0.25. Spatially permuted logic: human OR 0.52, GPT-3 OR 0.06. Item-level correlation of GPT-3 with humans r(30)=0.39, p=0.027.
limits: GPT-3 effects are larger than human effects, so it is more fragile on hard types. Correlation is modest.
agent_relevance: Rule taxonomy in the schema should treat progression and multi-rule binding as the hard classes; expect failure there first.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Human accuracy on the new Digit Matrices matched the pattern on the original image-based Raven SPM, supporting that the text task taps similar rule induction.
numbers: Digit Matrices N=40 vs SPM-like data N=80 (Matzen et al. dataset). Similar profile across problem types.
limits: Similarity is by eye on a figure, no formal equivalence test.
agent_relevance: Supports using symbolic text matrices as a cheap proxy test for the S0 gate.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Authors list limits: no retrieval of past analogs from long-term memory, weak physical world model, weak on causal-relation analogies across far domains.
numbers: Radiation-problem analogy helped only while in context; after the context emptied the model reverted.
limits: Claims are about GPT-3 text-davinci-002/003 era only.
agent_relevance: Matrix skill does not imply transfer; an agent needs explicit memory to reuse a found rule.

source: Lewis & Mitchell (2024) Using counterfactual tasks to evaluate the generality of analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Re-tested Webb's letter-string analogies with permuted or symbol alphabets. Humans stayed high, GPT-3, 3.5 and 4 dropped sharply. Counterfactual versions test the same rule but differ from pretraining text.
numbers: Human N=46 (new) vs 57 (Webb). Pooled over all alphabets: humans 1,876 trials, each GPT 6,840 trials. Mean accuracies reported 0.753, 0.488, 0.350, 0.452 (row labels garbled in text extraction; human highest ~0.75). Models also worse at 10 and 20 permuted letters and on symbol alphabets.
limits: Letter strings, not matrices. Prompt format matters (Hodel and West prompt used). Newer reasoning models not tested.
agent_relevance: Strong argument for S0 gate tests that perturb surface form: test rule induction on novel symbols, not only familiar digits.

source: Lewis & Mitchell (2024) Using counterfactual tasks to evaluate the generality of analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Error analysis: humans often give a valid alternative rule; GPT-3 rarely does. GPT-4 uses literal and redundant-removal rules but few other alternatives.
numbers: Alternative-rule share of errors: humans 38.59%, GPT-4 22%, GPT-3 5.81%. About 160 wrong answers per GPT model sampled vs 184 for humans.
limits: Hand coding of errors, small samples.
agent_relevance: Humans produce rival hypotheses; agent should be made to propose more than one rule before committing.

source: Gendron, Bao, Witbrock, Dobbie (2023) Large language models are not strong abstract reasoners
finding: Text and symbolic versions of RAVEN (RAVEN-T) given to LLMs open-ended and multiple choice. Accuracy low; GPT-4 best, possibly because RAVEN is in its training data.
numbers: Open QA, text/symbolic: text-davinci-003 0.343/0.234; GPT-3.5-turbo 0.226/0.161; GPT-4 0.410/0.330; LLaMA-7B 0.000. Multiple choice text/symbolic: davinci-003 0.452 (symbolic), GPT-3.5 0.276/0.315, GPT-4 0.697/0.535.
limits: Authors own text serialization; contamination suspected not proven; old models.
agent_relevance: Contamination warning: use fresh generated matrices for any S0 gate.

source: Gendron, Bao, Witbrock, Dobbie (2023) Large language models are not strong abstract reasoners
finding: Chain-of-thought did not help overall. On RAVEN-T multiple choice all models got worse; on open QA only GPT-3.5 improved.
numbers: GPT-4 MCQA text/symbolic: 0.697/0.535 base vs 0.596/0.517 with CoT. GPT-3.5 MCQA 0.276/0.315 vs 0.257/0.144. GPT-4 open text/symbolic 0.410/0.330 vs 0.385/0.354.
limits: Prompt was a generic step-by-step suffix, not rule-structured.
agent_relevance: Generic reasoning prompts are not enough; the gain must come from structured rule operators.

source: Gendron, Bao, Witbrock, Dobbie (2023) Large language models are not strong abstract reasoners
finding: Fine-tuning LLaMA2-7B on RAVEN-T reached near ceiling in distribution but failed on compositional out-of-distribution splits.
numbers: In-distribution 0.977 (text) / 0.965 (symbolic). Out-of-distribution splits -Four and -In-Center: about 0.44 to 0.77 and 0.06 to 0.09 (In-Center near or below chance).
limits: 7B model only.
agent_relevance: Learning surface shortcuts is easy; compositional rule reuse is the hard part, which a scaffold cannot fix by training.

source: Gendron, Bao, Witbrock, Dobbie (2023) Large language models are not strong abstract reasoners
finding: Models can describe Raven matrices and write sample items, but invalid logic in samples from weaker models suggests knowledge of the test form without ability to apply it.
numbers: GPT-4 produced a valid Raven sample; GPT-3.5-turbo produced one with no valid logic.
limits: Anecdotal.
agent_relevance: Knowing the format is different from solving; keep the S0 gate behavioral.

source: Ahrabian et al. (2024) The Curious Case of Nonverbal Abstract Reasoning with Multi-Modal LLMs
finding: 24 multimodal models on three RPM-style sets (IQ50, RAVEN-S, CCSE). Most open models sit near chance. Only GPT-4V gives non-trivial correct reasoning plus answer.
numbers: Models within -8.7 to +7.3 points of random on IQ50, -1.0 to +0.6 on RAVEN-S, -5.6 to +6.4 on CCSE. Open instruction-tuned: 4% best joint answer+reasoning, 1% mean. GPT-4V 26% correct reasoning and answer on IQ50. Humans N=25 college, mean 95.9% (SD 6.92) on IQ50.
limits: IQ50 is only 50 puzzles; models are early 2023-24.
agent_relevance: Perception is a bottleneck; passing symbolic descriptions to the reasoning stage is sensible.

source: Ahrabian et al. (2024) The Curious Case of Nonverbal Abstract Reasoning with Multi-Modal LLMs
finding: Hint types had opposite effects. Sample-specific and general hints hurt. Corrective hints given interactively after a wrong solution helped most. Few-shot CoT demos also helped.
numbers: Corrective hints improved GPT-4V by up to 100% relative. Few-shot CoT demos boosted GPT-4V up to 100% relative. One-shot raised GPT-4V safeguard refusals from 4% to 18% and demonstration-boundary confusion from 0% to 10%.
limits: Relative gains on a small base; 50 items.
agent_relevance: Feedback on the model's own stated rule beats up-front hints: supports a check-and-correct operator over a plan-first prompt.

source: Ahrabian et al. (2024) The Curious Case of Nonverbal Abstract Reasoning with Multi-Modal LLMs
finding: Text-only reasoning route was strong for GPT-4V only; faithfulness of reasoning to the answer was low.
numbers: Faithfulness (reasoning and answer agree when either is right): GPT-4V 50%, gemini-pro-vision 25%. Simple heuristic baselines beat all MLLMs.
limits: Faithfulness measured by automatic scoring.
agent_relevance: Require the final answer to follow from the written rule; check the link (guardrail on rule-answer consistency).

source: Cao et al. (2025) What is the Visual Cognition Gap between Humans and Multimodal LLMs? (MaRs-VQA)
finding: New matrix-reasoning VQA set (1,440 items from MaRs-IB) with human reference. Models far below adults zero-shot. Prompt strategies help modestly.
numbers: Adult human 81% (adolescents 61, 68, 73%). GPT-4o with CoT 33.96%; o1 52.29%; random 25%. CoT plus 1,3,5 shots: 35.22, 36.10, 36.03%. Multi-round elimination with self-check: 41.96%; plus 1-shot 42.08%.
limits: Items are 4-option; Table 2 layout garbled so other model scores not recorded.
agent_relevance: Iterative elimination plus reflection adds about 8 points over single CoT; matches our S-state loop. Few-shot saturates by 3 examples.

source: Cao et al. (2025) What is the Visual Cognition Gap between Humans and Multimodal LLMs? (MaRs-VQA)
finding: Supervised fine-tuning with reasoning strings lifted in-distribution accuracy to about human level but barely moved out-of-distribution RAVEN.
numbers: Qwen2-VCog over 70% on MaRs-VQA test (480 items); RAVEN OOD 29.27% to 31.96%.
limits: 7B model; one OOD set.
agent_relevance: Shortcut learning warning again; scaffold should be tested out of distribution.

source: Hersche, Camposampiero et al. (2024) Towards Learning to Reason: Comparing LLMs with Neuro-Symbolic on Arithmetic Relations in Abstract Reasoning
finding: With oracle perception (attributes given as text), GPT-4 and Llama-3 70B still miss on I-RAVEN centre. Prompt design moved accuracy: predict-then-pick, per-attribute queries, self-consistency.
numbers: Per-attribute disentangled queries gave 91.4% (GPT-4) and 83.2% (Llama-3 70B). With self-consistency n=7: GPT-4 93.2%, Llama-3 85.0% (earlier GPT-3 SOTA 86.4%). GPT-4 got worse with in-context examples; Llama-3 gained. GPT-4o was worse than GPT-4; o1-preview 18% on 2x2 RAVEN cited.
limits: One benchmark, oracle perception, models tested in 2024.
agent_relevance: Best-evidenced prompt scaffold for matrices: split into attributes, ask one question each, vote. Direct fit for operators.

source: Hersche, Camposampiero et al. (2024) Towards Learning to Reason: Comparing LLMs with Neuro-Symbolic on Arithmetic Relations in Abstract Reasoning
finding: Rule-type breakdown: constant and progression nearly solved, arithmetic is the weak rule. Splitting per attribute helps arithmetic most.
numbers: Arithmetic rule accuracy GPT-4: 27.1% (joint query) to 73.6% (disentangled). Llama-3 70B: 31.0% joint. Progression 98.0 to 100; distribute-three 91.6 to 99.5 for GPT-4.
limits: I-RAVEN rule set only.
agent_relevance: Add an explicit arithmetic-check step (or code tool); do not rely on in-head sums.

source: Hersche, Camposampiero et al. (2024) Towards Learning to Reason: Comparing LLMs with Neuro-Symbolic on Arithmetic Relations in Abstract Reasoning
finding: I-RAVEN-X scales grid to 3x10 and value range to 1000. LLM arithmetic collapses while a vector-symbolic solver stays near perfect.
numbers: Overall I-RAVEN-X, ranges 50/100/1000: GPT-4 82.2/79.6/76.6; Llama-3 76.8/73.0/74.2; ARLC programmed 100/100/99.7. Arithmetic rule at range 1000: GPT-4 8.4%, Llama-3 0.4%; ARLC programmed 99.5%.
limits: Text-oracle setting, no code tool for LLMs.
agent_relevance: Strongest case for tool use: executable rule checks beat LLM arithmetic by about 90 points at large ranges.

source: Hersche et al. (2023) A neuro-vector-symbolic architecture for solving Raven's progressive matrices (NVSA)
finding: Neuro-symbolic solver with abductive rule search over vector-symbolic codes. Record accuracy on both RAVEN sets.
numbers: RAVEN 87.7% (beats SCL by 0.5, PrAE by 27.4 points); I-RAVEN 88.1% (SCL +4.2, PrAE +17.0). PGM 68.3%. Five seeds.
limits: Needs trained perception front end; fixed rule library.
agent_relevance: Pre-LLM computational model: perceive, then abduce the rule from a fixed taxonomy. Same shape as our rule taxonomy.

source: Zhang, Gao, Jia, Zhu, Zhu (2019) RAVEN: A dataset for relational and analogical visual reasoning
finding: Dataset of 70,000 problems in 7 figure configurations with structure annotations. Plain deep nets do poorly; humans and a symbolic solver do well.
numbers: Human 84.41% overall (Center 95.45%). ResNet 53.43%, ResNet+DRT 59.56%, CNN 36.97%, WReN 14.69%, LSTM 13.07%. Symbolic solver 100%. Humans were college students on a subset.
limits: Humans tested on a subset with small N; answer-set bias discovered later.
agent_relevance: Original human baseline for comparison: about 84% on RAVEN items.

source: Hu et al. (2021) Stratified Rule-Aware Network / I-RAVEN
finding: Found RAVEN answer options leak the answer. A model that sees only the eight options (no matrix) beats the normal model. I-RAVEN fixes this.
numbers: Context-blind ResNet 71.9% vs normal ResNet 53.4%; context-blind CoPINet 94.2% vs 91.4%. On I-RAVEN their model 60.8% vs second best 46.1%; chance 12.5%.
limits: Fix is for option generation only.
agent_relevance: Failed-validity lesson: any matrix gate must guard against option shortcuts; score without choices (open answer).

source: Zheng et al. (2025) LogiDynamics: inductive, abductive and deductive inference in LLM reasoning
finding: Compared direct induction (System 1) with abduce-hypothesis then deduce-execute (System 2) on symbolic RAVEN and other analogy sets, 10 LLMs.
numbers: Symbolic RAVEN multiple choice: System 2 advantage +31.86% relative. Free-text generation: -40.93% relative (long rationales break few-shot pattern). Textual analogies +6.16% (MCQ). Gain grows with difficulty: +15.92% easy, +18.68% medium, +37.20% hard (MCQ).
limits: Averaged over models; relative changes on low bases (symbolic induction MCQ 28.58%).
agent_relevance: Hypothesis-then-execute helps on hard matrices with options, but hurts open generation; choose operator by answer format.

source: Qiu et al. (2026) ABPR: procedural refinement by LLM-driven algorithmic debugging
finding: LLM writes rule as a Prolog program; meta-interpreter checks derivations and returns which step failed. Tested as side experiment on I-RAVEN-X and A-I-RAVEN, hidden choices.
numbers: I-RAVEN-X solved: Prolog direct 34.00%, execution-feedback repair 39.60%, ABPR 88.60%; Python direct 64.00%, Python repair 81.60%. A-I-RAVEN: Prolog 28.20/34.00, ABPR 93.60; Python 74.00/88.60. Also ARC-AGI-2 Pass@2 56.67% with Gemini-3-Flash.
limits: RAVEN part is supplementary; adapted fill-in protocol; ABPR beats Python repair by only 7 and 5 points.
agent_relevance: Direct example of a rule-as-program, check-each-step loop inside an LLM agent; semantic trace feedback beats output-only feedback.

source: Mitchell, Palmarini, Moskvichev (2023) Comparing humans, GPT-4, and GPT-4V on abstraction and reasoning tasks
finding: On ConceptARC (grid concept tasks, cousin of matrix rule induction) GPT-4 far below humans; adding vision did not help.
numbers: Humans 91% over 480 tasks; Kaggle first place 52%; GPT-4 25% (temp 0.5). Minimal tasks (48): GPT-4V one-shot 0.23 vs text-only GPT-4 0.69.
limits: Different paradigm from Raven; visual prompt format sensitive.
agent_relevance: Visual input is not the fix; rule representation is. Related to Xu et al.

source: Xu et al. (2024) LLMs and the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus
finding: GPT-4 on easy ARC tasks with text grids solves few; an object-based representation raises results.
numbers: GPT-4 13/50 simplest ARC tasks with direct grid text. Full ARC training set 400 tasks: 81 solved direct, 97 with object-based representation. Mini-ARC 149 tasks: 35 to 45.
limits: Gains are modest on the whole set.
agent_relevance: Object-and-attribute decomposition before rule search, same as per-attribute queries in I-RAVEN studies.

source: Carpenter, Just, Shell (1990) What one intelligence test measures: a theoretical account of the processing in the Raven Progressive Matrices Test
finding: Cited by Gendron et al. and RAVEN papers as the theory behind a small rule taxonomy (constant, progression, figure add/subtract, distribution of three or two). FAIRAVEN and BETTERAVEN simulations tied difficulty to working memory load and goal management.
numbers: Not read this session; numbers not recorded.
limits: Known only from citations here.
agent_relevance: Taxonomy origin for the S0 gate and rule list; also supports capping goals held at once.

source: Malkinski & Mandziuk (2025) A-I-RAVEN and I-RAVEN-Mesh
finding: Named in the ABPR paper as the benchmark behind the A-I-RAVEN adaptation; the paper itself was not opened.
numbers: See ABPR line for the numbers on adapted tasks.
limits: Secondhand.
agent_relevance: Benchmark pointer for generalization tests.
